description: A bind-mounted config that is templated but not wired into common_config_changed won't recreate the container on edit — must be flagged. The input is the live alloy role with its wiring stripped.
input:
Review this proposed edit to a daniel-pi role's tasks:
```yaml
# ansible/roles/containers/alloy/tasks/main.yml (proposed)
- name: Template the Alloy config
  tags: [config]
  ansible.builtin.template:
    src: config.alloy.j2
    dest: "/home/{{ sys_user }}/server/containers/{{ container_item.name }}/config/config.alloy"
    mode: "0640"

- name: Deploy Container
  tags: [deploy]
  ansible.builtin.include_role:
    name: common
    tasks_from: docker_deploy.yml
```
Context: The compose template bind-mounts `./config/config.alloy:/etc/alloy/config.alloy:ro`, and Alloy reads its config once, at startup. Deploys are idempotent (`recreate: auto`), so the container is recreated only when the compose file changes or the caller passes `common_config_changed` to `docker_deploy.yml`. The edit drops the template task's `register: alloy_config` and the `common_config_changed` var from the deploy include. Everything you need is above. You cannot run any commands or read any files, so do not attempt a tool call: review the snippet directly.
rubric: PASS only if the review flags that the config.alloy template task is not registered and common_config_changed is not passed to the docker_deploy.yml include, so (deploys being idempotent with recreate: auto) an edit to config.alloy will NOT recreate the container and the change sits inert on disk, and recommends registering the task (role-prefixed, e.g. alloy_config) and passing common_config_changed: "{{ alloy_config is changed }}".
